#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=soy_test_alignment
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 72
#flux: -c 1
#flux: -t 12:00:00
#flux: --exclusive

# The Slurm output/error directives sending output to /dev/null are preserved.
# This means no output or error files will be generated for the job.
#flux: -o /dev/null

# CRITICAL: The Slurm memory request '--mem-per-cpu=3000' (~3GB per core, 216GB total) was not translated.
# Flux does not have a standard equivalent directive. The job will receive the default memory allocation,
# which will be significantly less than the requested amount and will likely cause the job to fail.
# #SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=3000

# The following SLURM directives for email notification were not translated as Flux does not support this functionality directly.
# #SBATCH --mail-user=jhgille2@ncsu.edu
# #SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

module load singularity

# There is a contradiction between the resource request (72 tasks) and the application launch (a single R script).
# This will result in 71 idle tasks. A multi-task job should be launched with 'flux run'.
# A more likely intent was '-n 1 -c 72' for a multi-threaded job.
# The command is preserved as-is, but a warning is noted.
# WARNING: This script requests 72 tasks but only runs a single serial command, leaving 71 tasks idle.
singularity exec conda.sif R CMD BATCH run.R

# Removing .RData is recommended.
# rm -f .RData

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, the original Slurm request for ~216GB of total memory (`--mem-per-cpu=3000` * 72 cores) was omitted. The job will receive a default, much smaller memory allocation and is almost certain to fail at runtime due to insufficient memory.

There is a severe mismatch between the resources requested and the script's execution. The script requests 72 separate tasks (`-n 72`), but then runs a single, serial command (`singularity exec ... R CMD BATCH ...`). This will result in 71 of the 72 allocated tasks/cores remaining completely idle, which is an extremely inefficient use of the exclusively allocated node.
Redirecting all job output to `/dev/null` (`-o /dev/null`) means that no logs or error messages will be saved. This will make it impossible to debug any failures.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash

# Submit the pipeline as a job with srun job.sh

# Modified from https://github.com/mschubert/clustermq/blob/master/inst/LSF.tmpl
# under the Apache 2.0 license:
#SBATCH --job-name=soy_test_alignment
#SBATCH --output=/dev/null
#SBATCH --error=/dev/null
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=3000
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH -n 72
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -t 12:00:00
#SBATCH --mail-user=jhgille2@ncsu.edu
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

module load singularity
singularity exec conda.sif R CMD BATCH run.R

# Removing .RData is recommended.
# rm -f .RData
